title: Maximum Number of Weeks for Which You Can Work
summary: Given an integer array milestones where each element represents the number of milestones for the corresponding project, you must complete exactly one milestone per week from any project, ensuring that you do not work on the same project for two consecutive weeks.
statement: Given an integer array milestones where each element represents the number of milestones for the corresponding project, you must complete exactly one milestone per week from any project, ensuring that you do not work on the same project for two consecutive weeks. The process stops when all milestones are completed or when continuing would violate the rules. Return the maximum number of weeks you can work on the projects without breaking the rules.
constraints: milestones has 1 through 100000 positive counts, each at most 1000000000.
Complete one milestone per week and never use the same project in consecutive weeks.
Return the maximum schedulable number of weeks; you may stop before every milestone is completed.
reference_solution:
def maximum_work_weeks(milestones):
    total = sum(milestones)
    largest = max(milestones)
    others = total - largest
    return total if largest <= others + 1 else 2 * others + 1

hints: Only the largest project can run out of separators; all smaller projects together supply those separators.
Let largest=M and others=S. If M<=S+1, schedule everything; otherwise alternate S other milestones with S+1 from the largest.

The balanced condition permits a full alternating arrangement. In the imbalanced case each non-largest milestone separates at most two largest-project weeks, proving both the upper bound and the alternating construction.
